title: The Scholarship of the quarry
premise: Theo Ravensworth, a scholarship student hiding her family's bankruptcy and her own anxiety behind careful invisibility, arrives at Hollowmere Academy, built atop an abandoned slate quarry where a girl named Wren Halloway died in 1911. When the school ghost begins leaving Theo notes in ink that appears on no known substance, Theo realizes Wren was silenced after uncovering a theft ring among the founders' descendants — and that the same families still control the school, and are quietly expelling scholarship students like Theo to cover new crimes. As Theo and her found family of misfits dig into the quarry's sealed records, she must choose between the safe anonymity she craves and testifying to what she knows, even though the last student who spoke up drowned. In the end, Theo exposes the modern conspiracy at the centenary gala, Wren's name is restored to the school's memorial wall, and Theo stops being fine — she becomes someone who is heard.
about_author: P. M. Villalobos is the pen name of a former boarding-school archivist who spent years cataloguing letters from students who never came home. They write stories about kids who refuse to be footnotes.

chapters.title: Fine Is a Load-Bearing Word
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. She arrives at Hollowmere Academy on a scholarship, rehearsing her invisibility strategy: head down, grades up, no attachments. A tour guide mentions the quarry ghost as a joke. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as control.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Fell Upward
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In history class she learns of Wren Halloway, who died in the quarry in 1911 — officially an accident, unofficially never discussed. The teacher changes the subject when Theo asks how. Beat: first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Ink That Isn't Ink
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. She finds a note in her locker: 'You ask good questions, Theo Ravensworth.' The writing shimmers like oil on water and won't photograph. Beat: fear mixed with a thrilling sense of being seen.

chapters.title: The Misfit Table
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Chased by a note's implications, she sits with the scholarship kids: Priya the codebreaker, Marcus the expelled-swimmer, June who hears humming near the quarry fence. Beat: reluctant first bonds of found family.

chapters.title: Rules of the Quarry
chapters.summary: June's POV. June shows Theo the fence line where compasses spin and her phone dies; locals say the quarry 'keeps what it's owed.' They find a 1912 disciplinary ledger page half-buried in slate. Beat: dread deepening into purpose.

chapters.title: Second Note, First Threat
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A second note names three expelled scholarship students across decades — all 'left suddenly.' Headmaster Voss catches Theo in the archive and warns her about 'obsessions.' Beat: the institution reveals its teeth.

chapters.title: Priya Runs the Numbers
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers all three expelled students held the same endowed scholarship — funded by the Ashcombe family, whose name is on both the 1911 quarry deed and Theo's own award letter. Beat: past and present snap together.

chapters.title: What Wren Knew
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. In the boathouse, the ghost's notes lead them to Wren's hidden journal: she'd caught the founders' sons stealing quarry wages and framing workers. Her 'accident' came days later. Beat: grief and fury on behalf of a dead girl.

chapters.title: The Humming
chapters.summary: June's POV. June finally follows the humming to a bricked-up mine shaft and comes back shaking, holding a slate chalkboard with Wren's handwriting: 'Tell them I counted.' Beat: the ghost is real, and she is not vengeful — she is waiting.

chapters.title: Labels Come Off
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Voss puts Theo on academic probation for 'unauthorized archival access,' threatening her scholarship. Her parents' financial ruin nearly surfaces publicly. Beat: the cost of survival made personal; invisibility failing completely.

chapters.title: The Ashcombe Gala Invitation
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The centenary gala approaches; Theo is assigned to serve refreshments — the scholarship kids' traditional role. She accepts, planning to use access, not hide. Beat: turning fear into strategy.

chapters.title: Someone Else Knows
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus finds evidence someone else has been reading Wren's journal pages before them — pages now missing. A faculty ally, Ms. Okafor, hints she lost her job once already for asking questions. Beat: paranoia; the enemy is inside.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Archive
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Following a forged note, Theo is nearly caught breaking into restricted records; Priya's quick thinking saves her, but they realize the notes have split — some from Wren, some bait from their enemies. Beat: trust tested within the group.

chapters.title: Wren Speaks
chapters.summary: June's POV. At the shaft, through June, Wren communicates in chalk and cold air: the missing ledger page proving the wage theft is behind the brick, and so is proof of the modern scheme — Ashcombes have been diverting scholarship endowments for generations. Beat: awe and resolve.

chapters.title: Breaking the Seal
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The four break the shaft seal at night. Inside: Wren's remains respectfully recovered long ago, but her tin box survives — ledger page, stolen wage receipts, and a letter naming every descendant complicit. Beat: solemnity; touching history's wound.

chapters.title: Voss Closes In
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Voss searches dorms, confiscates the decoy box Priya planted, and suspends Marcus and June. He offers Theo a deal: silence and graduation, or expulsion like the others. Beat: the price of survival stated plainly.

chapters.title: What Theo Ravensworth Decides
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Alone with Wren's letter, Theo confronts why she hides: shame that isn't hers. She chooses testimony over safety, copying the evidence and mailing copies to trustees, press, and Ms. Okafor. Beat: quiet, irreversible courage.

chapters.title: The Centenary Gala
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. During the founder's toast, the lights fail, the quarry hums, and Wren's ink blooms across the ballroom's commemorative banner: 'I COUNTED. ASK THEO RAVENSWORTH.' Beat: climax ignites; the dead refuse erasure.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Before two hundred guests, Theo presents the ledger, the endowment records, and the pattern of expulsions. Voss tries to discredit her; Okafor and a shaken trustee corroborate. Beat: the terrifying relief of being fully visible.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Voss resigns under investigation; the Ashcombe endowment is frozen and rebuilt with student oversight. Marcus and June are reinstated. But the board hesitates on one item: restoring Wren's name. Beat: victory incomplete, justice unfinished.

chapters.title: The Wall
chapters.summary: June's POV. At dawn by the quarry, the four hold a small ceremony. When they hang Wren's name on the memorial wall themselves, the humming stops — replaced, June says, by something like singing. Beat: release; the found family holds.

chapters.title: Not Fine, Better
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Epilogue in spring: Theo writes her college essay truthfully, signs her name without flinching, and finds one last note in her locker — just 'Thank you,' in ordinary fading ink, the ghost finally at rest. Beat: peace earned, identity claimed.
